entries.result: One exact pre-Resolve record selected vtable 0x82047628 and its +0x0C provider 0x82517800.
The provider exports wrapper +0x14 as its first output, zeroes its second output, and returns one.
The static factory, publication, reference-count, cleanup, and dynamic lower-release paths are bounded, and the accepted run joins one runtime wrapper/resource token to this factory and its creator.

The alternate factory pre-call supplies r4/r5 from source/context virtual +0x48/+0x4C results, r6 literal 1, r7 from configuration +0x0C after its bounded conditional patch, and r8 literal 0. Only r7 low-six-bit values 0x06 and 0x36 receive accepted Xenos format names; all other roles remain qualified.

Seven accepted matches join the alternate pre-call token to creator 0x82533DB8 and selected-slot-equals-r6; the three observed input sets are 0x400/0x400/1/0x18280106/0, 0x500/0x2D0/1/0x28280106/0, and 0x500/0x2D0/1/0x1A200136/0.

The matched creator allocates a 0x34-byte result, forwards extents and derived controls through the builder chain, and applies the page-base patch; exact per-set header words, requested sizes, and backing identity remain unobserved.

The sole exact diagnostic-string reference associates 0x8252EF20 with NiXenonRenderedTextureData::Create and nested NiXenonTextureBufferData::Create failure. The created lower resource is stored at outer +0x58, and the immediate caller registers the owning object through a generic hash-table insert/update.

Two adjacent NiXenonRenderer table methods obtain an outer data object, read its +0x58 lower resource, and pass it through a paired layout/location and page-base path while toggling outer virtual +0x60. This is a CPU-access-like static boundary; no accepted alternate Resolve token is dynamically joined to it.

Stable-menu tokens 2, 5, and 6 each joined exact alternate creation to a live Resolve, but none produced an exact consumer-open or consumer-close row. The result is bounded to the accepted run and does not prove global unreachability.

Five untruncated same-displacement call shapes were found. Two cannot provide a meaningful exact target traversal, fixed receiver 0x8314F76C has a distinct installed vtable, and two close shapes remain without receiver-vtable identity. No owner-visible runtime sequence is statically supported.

The fixed receiver is initialized with distinct vtable 0x82138768, whose +0x11C entry is 0x82D7ED00. The same receiver dispatch at 0x82E28A70 is therefore excluded as a caller of NiXenonRenderer method 0x8250E0F0 in the proved initialized state.

conclusion: One exact pre-Resolve runtime record selected vtable 0x82047628 and provider 0x82517800. That provider returns selected-wrapper field +0x14 as the first output that reaches Resolve r6, writes zero as its second output, and returns true. The accepted creator-input run joins the alternate factory pre-call 0x82517FFC to creator 0x82533DB8 for seven records and three input sets. Outer creator 0x8252EF20 is associated with NiXenonRenderedTextureData::Create and stores the lower resource at outer +0x58. NiXenonRenderer methods 0x8250E0F0 and 0x8250E1D0 are the first concrete non-cleanup consumers of that field, but the consumed stable-menu run joined exact alternate creation and Resolve tokens 2, 5, and 6 to neither method. A decoded scan found five same-displacement virtual-call shapes. Fixed receiver 0x8314F76C is now excluded: initializer 0x82D7E758 installs distinct vtable 0x82138768, whose +0x11C target is 0x82D7ED00 rather than 0x8250E0F0. Two meaningful close shapes remain without receiver-vtable identity, so no owner-visible sequence is supported. The next discriminator is a static provenance trace for the registry receiver returned by 0x82CAAAA8 at callsite 0x82CAE220. Original method names, concrete lower class, offscreen or render-target use, Scaleform or GFx ownership, presentation identity, input semantics beyond the accepted numeric boundary, exact per-set header/size values, mutation or contents generation, lower allocation/free, and address recycling remain unresolved.
